raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Distribute MHC prenorm bucket compilation across ranks sharing a TileLang cache using two passes: claim available buckets, then wait for deferred buckets and replay outside the lock. Every rank still materializes all kernels; kernel math, bucket selection, and prewarm timing are unchanged.

- Locks use TileLang's resolved `TILELANG_CACHE_DIR` and include GPU architecture in the bucket key.
- mkdir/open/flock/unlock/close failures fall back to independent prewarm, with one warning per process. Lock-contention waits are bounded to 300 seconds per bucket.
- Owner death releases the OS lock. Recovery or timeout may cause concurrent compilation; there is no single-waiter takeover guarantee.

## Validation

Three CPU tests pass: multiprocess claim/wait/release, bounded waiting, and parameterized lock failures that preserve full-bucket replay and propagate replay exceptions. Pre-commit checks pass.

Existing DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 results from the original patch (not rerun for this reliability update):

| Hardware | MHC prewarm before → after | Startup to first response before → after |
|---|---|---|
| B200 TP8 | 158.6s → 31.4s | 442.7s → 316.3s |
| GB300 TP4 | 286.0s → 81.3s | 725.5s → 518.8s |

Warm-cache prewarm was ~2.6s either way. Four deterministic DSPARK prompts produced identical text, acceptance lengths, and verification counts.

GPU cold/warm-cache reruns and real cross-node shared-filesystem validation remain outstanding. Read-only filesystem failures are covered by EROFS injection. The timeout cannot interrupt filesystem calls stuck inside the OS, and TileLang's own cache/compiler errors remain outside this helper.

nodes.body: A small update to my review: I closed #44104 for now, so its text conflict with this PR is gone. If this lands, I will reopen it so GLM gets the gain, and rename the "DeepSeek V4" log line then.

With this PR and my #44104 applied, GLM-5.3-Flash cold ready time goes from 590 s to 400 s at TP4 on B200 (one run each). The gain is in the prewarm hook, which drops from 252 s on #44104 alone to 70 s, with each rank claiming 5 to 7 of 22 buckets.

| Tree | Ready | Prewarm hook | Prefill graph capture | GSM8K |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 590 s | none | 281 s | 98.0% |
| #44104 | 580 s | 252 s | 44 s | 99.0% |
| #44104 and this PR | 400 s | 70 s | 43 s | 98.5% |

Settings: 4 B200s, real GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 weights in the page cache, and the recipe from `test/registered/e2e/models/test_glm53_flash_b200.py` (TP4, EAGLE 5/1/6, FP8 KV, trtllm DSA, flashinfer_trtllm MoE). The cookbook recipe uses `--tp-size 8`, but I had 4 GPUs. All JIT caches were empty (`TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `TILELANG_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR`). The base was main 582168dd7c, with #44104 at f8f94b1b40. GSM8K is sgl-eval 0.1.3 with 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max tokens 32768, and `--thinking`. The gaps are at most 2 questions in one run per tree.

An earlier run of the two-PR tree also reached ready in 400 s. `bench_serving` at 4096 input tokens, 256 output tokens, and concurrency 1 was about the same on all three trees. The first sweep after ready took 24.1 s, 23.9 s, and 23.7 s, since this recipe's prefill graph capture already compiles these kernels.

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 without #44104, the prewarm hook (`_prewarm_mhc_kernels`) goes from about 240 s to about 70 s and cold ready goes from 695 s to 465 s, one run each. That is 4 B200s with the cookbook flash-official low-latency flags at `--tp 4` (the cookbook uses `--tp 8`). On a warm cache, the hook takes about 2 s. GSM8K was 98.0% on main and 96.5% on this PR (sgl-eval, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, max tokens 32768, `--thinking`). The gap is 3 questions in one run per tree. This PR does not change kernel code, so I do not read the gap as a regression, but I did not repeat the eval.

I would fix one thing before merge. With `--enable-symm-mem` at TP4 and no DP attention, startup stalls in the prewarm. The inline comment has the evidence and a small change that removes the stall and keeps the gain.

The lock handling held up under every fault I injected: owner SIGKILL, stuck owner, missing cache directory, read-only path, per-rank caches, and virtiofs. No rank skipped a bucket, and after the prewarm, `mhc_pre` calls from 1 to 8192 tokens triggered no new compile. The unit test does not protect the bucket property yet, so I left a suggestion inline.

This PR has a text conflict with #44104 on the prewarm log line. Whichever lands second should also remove "DeepSeek V4" from the new "claimed" log line, because GLM reaches that line through #44104.

Not checked:
- Several nodes. I had one worker, so I did not test flock across nodes, NFS, or Lustre. By trace, if flock is node-local or fails on a shared cache, ranks compile concurrently and atomic rename handles the race.
- TP8, GB300, and the AMD `gcnArchName` key. I did not reproduce your TP8 and GB300 numbers.
- sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.5.post3, which upstream/main pins. My DeepSeek runs used 0.2.3.post2.
- This PR with weights read cold from storage. An earlier pair in that setup gave 760 s on main and 760 s on #44104, without this PR.

With `--enable-symm-mem` at TP4 and no DP attention, this stalls startup. Each rank now replays buckets in its own order, and `mhc_pre` allocates `layer_input` from the symmetric pool. That pool still grows here, because the prewarm runs before `prealloc_symmetric_memory_pool`. So ranks call the collective `ncclCommWindowRegister` with different sizes and different call counts. Main avoids this because all ranks replay in the same order.

A rank that finishes waits in `tp_group.barrier()` while its peers wait in the registration. The registration has no timeout. The barrier uses the gloo `cpu_group`, which defaults to 120 minutes, so a rank in the barrier should raise after about that long. I did not run a stall that long, so I expect a very long stall and then an error.

Evidence on 4 B200s with cold caches:
- Real server, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, cookbook flash-official low-latency flags at `--tp 4` plus `--enable-symm-mem`: main was ready in 670 s. This PR was not ready at my 840 s limit, and the log had no error. TP rank 1 logged "claimed 7 buckets, 15 held by peers", and the other ranks never logged that line.
- A script that runs `_prewarm_mhc_kernels` on real ranks with random weights: on main, all ranks registered the same sizes in the same order. On this PR, in the first collective step, one rank registered 2 MiB and the other three registered 20 MiB. Stack dumps then showed some ranks in `barrier` and the others in the registration under `mhc_pre`. The run was still stuck at my 900 s limit.
- The same script on a warm cache never finished within a 240 s limit.

I suggest keeping the prewarm out of the symmetric pool. The comment above `_dp_max_padding` in `dp_attention.py` already says the prewarm does not need it.

```python
# mhc_pre signature (keyword-only)
symmetric_output: bool = True,

# layer_input allocation in mhc_pre
disabled=not symmetric_output or not is_allocation_symmetric()

# mhc_pre call in replay()
symmetric_output=False,
```

With this change and `--enable-symm-mem` on cold caches, the real server had a hook time of 67 to 70 s and was ready in 465 s. Four fixed prompts at temperature 0 returned the same text as main. The script registered no windows during the prewarm.

`--enable-symm-mem` is not in the DeepSeek-V4 or GLM-5.3-Flash cookbook recipes, so those recipes do not reach this, but it is a documented server argument. One DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook recipe sets it together with DP attention, and by trace DP attention skips the pool at load.

Not checked for this stall: TP2 and TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash with both PRs (same helper, so by trace I expect the same stall), DP attention beyond the trace, main and the suggested change on a warm cache, and whether a run where window counts happen to match could give wrong collective results. The stack dumps come from the script. For the real server I only have the log and the missed ready limit.

This test only reaches the path where `own` is True, and the other tests call the claim helper directly, so nothing covers the second pass of `prewarm_mhc_pre`. I removed the second-pass `replay`, then the second-pass wait, then the `taken_by_peers` append, one at a time, and the suite still passed each time (Python 3.12 on macOS).

No rank skipped a bucket in my runs, so this only adds a guard for the contract that every rank materializes every kernel. I suggest adding a test where a child process holds the real lock on the m128 bucket and `prewarm_mhc_pre` runs with `mhc_pre` mocked. It can assert that the replay order is [64, 128] and that the 128 replay waits for the release. I tried this test, and it fails on each of those changes. I did not run those changes on Linux CI.

+
+@contextmanager
+def _claim_prewarm_bucket(
+    tag: str, *, wait: bool, timeout: float = 300.0
+) -> Iterator[bool]:
+    # False means a peer owns the bucket. Infrastructure failures yield True
+    # so this rank replays normally, without relying on another rank's cache.
+    lock_file = None
+    locked = False
+    own = True
+    try:
+        try:
+            import fcntl
+
+            from tilelang.env import env as tilelang_env
+
+            lock_dir = Path(tilelang_env.TILELANG_CACHE_DIR) / "prewarm_locks"
+            lock_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+            lock_file = open(lock_dir / f"{tag}.lock", "a")
+            deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+            while True:
+                try:
+                    fcntl.flock(lock_file, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
+                    locked = True
+                    break
+                except BlockingIOError:
+                    if not wait:
+                        own = False
+                        break
+                    # A live but stuck owner must not indefinitely delay startup.
+                    if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+                        _warn_prewarm_lock_fallback()
+                        break
+                    time.sleep(0.1)

+            _warn_prewarm_lock_fallback()
+        # Keep replay exceptions outside the lock error handler.
+        yield own
+    finally:
+        if locked:
+            try:
+                fcntl.flock(lock_file, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

inline_comments.body:
With `--enable-symm-mem` at TP4 and no DP attention, this stalls startup. Each rank now replays buckets in its own order, and `mhc_pre` allocates `layer_input` from the symmetric pool. That pool still grows here, because the prewarm runs before `prealloc_symmetric_memory_pool`. So ranks call the collective `ncclCommWindowRegister` with different sizes and different call counts. Main avoids this because all ranks replay in the same order.

A rank that finishes waits in `tp_group.barrier()` while its peers wait in the registration. The registration has no timeout. The barrier uses the gloo `cpu_group`, which defaults to 120 minutes, so a rank in the barrier should raise after about that long. I did not run a stall that long, so I expect a very long stall and then an error.

Evidence on 4 B200s with cold caches:
- Real server, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, cookbook flash-official low-latency flags at `--tp 4` plus `--enable-symm-mem`: main was ready in 670 s. This PR was not ready at my 840 s limit, and the log had no error. TP rank 1 logged "claimed 7 buckets, 15 held by peers", and the other ranks never logged that line.
- A script that runs `_prewarm_mhc_kernels` on real ranks with random weights: on main, all ranks registered the same sizes in the same order. On this PR, in the first collective step, one rank registered 2 MiB and the other three registered 20 MiB. Stack dumps then showed some ranks in `barrier` and the others in the registration under `mhc_pre`. The run was still stuck at my 900 s limit.
- The same script on a warm cache never finished within a 240 s limit.

I suggest keeping the prewarm out of the symmetric pool. The comment above `_dp_max_padding` in `dp_attention.py` already says the prewarm does not need it.

```python
# mhc_pre signature (keyword-only)
symmetric_output: bool = True,

# layer_input allocation in mhc_pre
disabled=not symmetric_output or not is_allocation_symmetric()

# mhc_pre call in replay()
symmetric_output=False,
```

With this change and `--enable-symm-mem` on cold caches, the real server had a hook time of 67 to 70 s and was ready in 465 s. Four fixed prompts at temperature 0 returned the same text as main. The script registered no windows during the prewarm.

`--enable-symm-mem` is not in the DeepSeek-V4 or GLM-5.3-Flash cookbook recipes, so those recipes do not reach this, but it is a documented server argument. One DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook recipe sets it together with DP attention, and by trace DP attention skips the pool at load.

Not checked for this stall: TP2 and TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash with both PRs (same helper, so by trace I expect the same stall), DP attention beyond the trace, main and the suggested change on a warm cache, and whether a run where window counts happen to match could give wrong collective results. The stack dumps come from the script. For the real server I only have the log and the missed ready limit.

I removed the second-pass `replay`, then the second-pass wait, then the `taken_by_peers` append, one at a time, and the suite still passed each time (Python 3.12 on macOS).

No rank skipped a bucket in my runs, so this only adds a guard for the contract that every rank materializes every kernel. I suggest adding a test where a child process holds the real lock on the m128 bucket and `prewarm_mhc_pre` runs with `mhc_pre` mocked. It can assert that the replay order is [64, 128] and that the 128 replay waits for the release. I tried this test, and it fails on each of those changes. I did not run those changes on Linux CI.

reviews.body:
With this PR and my #44104 applied, GLM-5.3-Flash cold ready time goes from 590 s to 400 s at TP4 on B200 (one run each). The gain is in the prewarm hook, which drops from 252 s on #44104 alone to 70 s, with each rank claiming 5 to 7 of 22 buckets.

| Tree | Ready | Prewarm hook | Prefill graph capture | GSM8K |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main | 590 s | none | 281 s | 98.0% |
| #44104 | 580 s | 252 s | 44 s | 99.0% |
| #44104 and this PR | 400 s | 70 s | 43 s | 98.5% |

Settings: 4 B200s, real GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 weights in the page cache, and the recipe from `test/registered/e2e/models/test_glm53_flash_b200.py` (TP4, EAGLE 5/1/6, FP8 KV, trtllm DSA, flashinfer_trtllm MoE). The cookbook recipe uses `--tp-size 8`, but I had 4 GPUs. All JIT caches were empty (`TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `TILELANG_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR`). The base was main 582168dd7c, with #44104 at f8f94b1b40. GSM8K is sgl-eval 0.1.3 with 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, max tokens 32768, and `--thinking`. The gaps are at most 2 questions in one run per tree.

An earlier run of the two-PR tree also reached ready in 400 s. `bench_serving` at 4096 input tokens, 256 output tokens, and concurrency 1 was about the same on all three trees. The first sweep after ready took 24.1 s, 23.9 s, and 23.7 s, since this recipe's prefill graph capture already compiles these kernels.

On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 without #44104, the prewarm hook (`_prewarm_mhc_kernels`) goes from about 240 s to about 70 s and cold ready goes from 695 s to 465 s, one run each. That is 4 B200s with the cookbook flash-official low-latency flags at `--tp 4` (the cookbook uses `--tp 8`). On a warm cache, the hook takes about 2 s. GSM8K was 98.0% on main and 96.5% on this PR (sgl-eval, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, max tokens 32768, `--thinking`). The gap is 3 questions in one run per tree. This PR does not change kernel code, so I do not read the gap as a regression, but I did not repeat the eval.

I would fix one thing before merge. With `--enable-symm-mem` at TP4 and no DP attention, startup stalls in the prewarm. The inline comment has the evidence and a small change that removes the stall and keeps the gain.

The lock handling held up under every fault I injected: owner SIGKILL, stuck owner, missing cache directory, read-only path, per-rank caches, and virtiofs. No rank skipped a bucket, and after the prewarm, `mhc_pre` calls from 1 to 8192 tokens triggered no new compile. The unit test does not protect the bucket property yet, so I left a suggestion inline.

This PR has a text conflict with #44104 on the prewarm log line. Whichever lands second should also remove "DeepSeek V4" from the new "claimed" log line, because GLM reaches that line through #44104.

Not checked:
- Several nodes. I had one worker, so I did not test flock across nodes, NFS, or Lustre. By trace, if flock is node-local or fails on a shared cache, ranks compile concurrently and atomic rename handles the race.
- TP8, GB300, and the AMD `gcnArchName` key. I did not reproduce your TP8 and GB300 numbers.
- sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.5.post3, which upstream/main pins. My DeepSeek runs used 0.2.3.post2.
- This PR with weights read cold from storage. An earlier pair in that setup gave 760 s on main and 760 s on #44104, without this PR.
